claim: Across 36 experimental configurations (4 models x 9 benchmarks), multi-agent debate (MAD) frameworks beat plain Chain-of-Thought in only about 15% of cases under ANOVA-tested Win/Tie/Lose categorization.
stance_target: multi-agent debate/critique reliably improves over single-model baselines
scope_conditions: 5 MAD frameworks (SoM, MP, EoT, ChatEval, AgentVerse), 4 foundation models, 9 benchmarks spanning general knowledge, math reasoning, and programming
quoted_support: SoM, EoT, ChatEval, and AgentVerse only outperformed CoT in approximately 15% cases, while MP did not demonstrate significant improvement over CoT.

claim: MAD frameworks perform worse specifically on programming tasks relative to other task types; only SoM and AgentVerse had positive win rates on programming, while MAD outperformed its own baseline more on mathematical reasoning.
stance_target: adversarial/debate-style multi-agent review is effective for code-defect catching
scope_conditions: HumanEval, MBPP programming benchmarks, same 4-model x 9-benchmark design
quoted_support: MAD frameworks performed worse on programming tasks (only SoM/AgentVerse had positive win rates) but better on mathematical reasoning, surpassing their overall performance levels.

claim: The one case where a MAD framework (AgentVerse) beat CoT on HumanEval is attributable not to debate/critique dynamics but to an added execution-evaluation stage where agents can run code and see test results -- a mechanism the authors say is 'arguably beyond the scope of MAD designs.'
stance_target: mechanism of apparent multi-agent code-quality gains
quoted_support: when handling programming tasks, AgentVerse incorporates an additional execution-evaluation stage so that agents can utilize the execution results from the generated programs, which is usually absent in other MAD frameworks and arguably beyond the scope of MAD designs.

claim: Increasing debate rounds (2-4) or agent population (3-9) does not fix the shortfall of debate frameworks on HumanEval; SoM continues to underperform CoT regardless of scaling these hyperparameters.
stance_target: scaling multi-agent debate interaction (more rounds/agents) improves code-defect catching
scope_conditions: Ablation study on HumanEval with SoM framework, debate rounds and agent count varied
quoted_support: the SoM framework continues to underperform CoT on the MMLU and HumanEval benchmarks, even as debate rounds increase from 2 to 4 or the number of agents increases from 3 to 9 on HumanEval.
